foods.name: Apple
foods.notes: Fructose and sorbitol together make apple a strong double trigger.

foods.name: Avocado
foods.notes: Limit strictly to 1/8 of a whole; a full avocado is high FODMAP.
foods.swap: Olive oil or cucumber for healthy fat

foods.name: Banana
foods.notes: Unripe/green banana is lower FODMAP; very ripe banana may edge into medium.

foods.name: Blackberries
foods.notes: Low at up to 40g. Larger servings become moderate to high.

foods.name: Cherry
foods.notes: Very high in sorbitol; even the small serving here affects many people.

foods.name: Dried cranberries
foods.notes: Concentrated fructose from drying plus often sweetened with apple juice or HFCS.

foods.name: Honeydew melon
foods.notes: Honeydew is high in excess fructose. Despite being a melon, it is not safe like cantaloupe.

foods.name: Persimmon
foods.notes: High in excess fructose.

foods.name: Watermelon
foods.notes: One of the highest FODMAP fruits; even small servings affect many people.

foods.name: Black beans
foods.notes: Low FODMAP only at 1/4 cup (45g) canned and rinsed. Larger servings quickly become High due to GOS content.

foods.name: Broccoli
foods.notes: Florets at this serving are fine; stalks may contain slightly more fructans.

foods.name: Brussels sprouts
foods.notes: Low FODMAP at just 2 sprouts. A typical side-dish portion (1/2 cup) is High - serving size matters critically here.

foods.name: Cabbage (common)
foods.notes: Savoy cabbage is higher; bok choy is a safe low-FODMAP swap. Common/red cabbage is safe up to 3/4 cup - beyond that fructan load becomes High.

foods.name: Cabbage (red)
foods.notes: Safe up to 3/4 cup. Larger portions push fructan content into High territory - serving size matters critically here.

foods.name: Cauliflower
foods.notes: Low at 1/2 cup of florets. A full cup or more is High in fructans and mannitol.

foods.name: Celery
foods.notes: Low FODMAP only below 5cm of stalk. A full stalk or more contains significant mannitol and becomes High.

foods.name: Chickpeas (canned, rinsed)
foods.notes: Rinsing removes much of the GOS. Larger servings or home-cooked become medium or high.

foods.name: Garlic
foods.notes: Even 1 clove is high. Use garlic-infused oil instead - FODMAPs do not leach into oil.

foods.name: Kidney beans
foods.notes: High FODMAP even at small servings. Canned and rinsed red kidney beans may be tolerated at 1/4 cup by some.

foods.name: Leek (leaves only)
foods.notes: Use only the green leaf portion; the white bulb is high in fructans.

foods.name: Lentils (canned, rinsed)
foods.notes: Canned and well rinsed only; home-cooked or larger portions are high.

foods.name: Mushrooms
foods.notes: Mannitol is very high in most mushroom varieties.
foods.swap: Zucchini or bell pepper for similar texture

foods.name: Onion
foods.notes: One of the most common IBS triggers. Scallion greens are a safe substitute.

foods.name: Scallion (green tips)
foods.notes: Green tops only; the white bulb contains fructans.

foods.name: Snow peas
foods.notes: Low at 5 pods (25g) only. A larger handful is High in fructans and GOS. Green beans are a more forgiving alternative.

foods.name: Sweet potato
foods.notes: Mannitol content rises with serving size; safe at up to 1/2 cup (75g). A full baked sweet potato is High FODMAP.

foods.name: Tomato
foods.notes: Cherry tomatoes may be slightly higher per serving due to concentrated fructose.

foods.name: Gluten-free pasta
foods.notes: Check ingredients; pasta made with legume flour may contain GOS.

foods.name: Granola
foods.notes: Most granola contains honey, dried fruit, and wheat - all high FODMAP. Check for low-FODMAP certified brands.

foods.name: Pasta (wheat)
foods.notes: Low at up to 1/2 cup cooked only. A standard restaurant-sized bowl of wheat pasta is High in fructans - use gluten-free or rice noodles for larger meals.

foods.name: Sourdough (white)
foods.notes: Long fermentation breaks down fructans. Must be a traditionally made sourdough.

foods.name: Wheat bread
foods.notes: Low at 1 slice only due to residual fructans. Two or more slices push it into High - choose sourdough or gluten-free for larger portions.

foods.name: Beef
foods.notes: Plain cooked only; avoid pre-seasoned versions with garlic or onion.

foods.name: Chicken
foods.notes: Plain cooked only; marinades with garlic or onion add FODMAPs.

foods.name: Chorizo
foods.notes: Plain pork chorizo is Low FODMAP, but many brands add garlic or onion powder - always check the ingredient list.

foods.name: Silken tofu
foods.notes: Unlike firm tofu, silken tofu retains most of the GOS from soy beans.

foods.name: Tempeh
foods.notes: Fermentation significantly reduces FODMAPs.

foods.name: Tofu (firm)
foods.notes: Firm tofu only; silken tofu is higher in GOS.

foods.name: Almond milk
foods.notes: Check label for added inulin or chicory root extract, which add FODMAPs.

foods.name: Butter
foods.notes: Almost pure fat with negligible lactose; safe for most lactose-sensitive people.

foods.name: Cheddar cheese
foods.notes: Hard aged cheeses are very low in lactose due to the fermentation process.

foods.name: Greek yogurt (plain)
foods.notes: Straining removes most lactose; full-fat plain is best. Low at a generous serving. Avoid flavoured varieties.

foods.name: Ice cream
foods.swap: Lactose-free ice cream or fruit sorbet (check ingredients)

foods.name: Oat milk
foods.notes: Many brands add inulin; check ingredients carefully. Low only at 30ml (for cereal); a full glass-sized pour is High in fructans.

foods.name: Ricotta cheese
foods.notes: Low at 2 tbsp only. Ricotta retains significant lactose - a larger serving (e.g. in lasagna) is High.

foods.name: Sour cream
foods.notes: Low at up to 2 tbsp. Larger servings are High due to lactose.

foods.name: Almonds
foods.notes: Low FODMAP at exactly 10 almonds (12g). Beyond this, GOS and fructan content rises sharply into High territory.

foods.name: Cashews
foods.notes: Even the small serving listed here is high FODMAP; best avoided entirely.

foods.name: Apple juice
foods.notes: High fructose even in small amounts; best avoided.
foods.swap: Water with lemon or orange juice (max 1/2 cup)

foods.name: Chamomile tea
foods.notes: Chamomile flowers are high in fructans. A common surprise trigger for IBS sufferers.

foods.name: Coconut water
foods.notes: Contains sorbitol; even 100ml may bother sensitive individuals. Use caution.

foods.name: Coffee (black)
foods.notes: Black coffee is low FODMAP; milky coffees depend on the milk used.

foods.name: Fennel tea
foods.notes: Made from fennel seeds, which are high in fructans at tea-strength concentration.

foods.name: Kombucha
foods.notes: Low at up to 180ml. Larger serves become High due to fructose from fermentation.

foods.name: Orange juice
foods.notes: Limit to 1/2 cup; a full glass can tip into high fructose territory.
foods.swap: Water with lemon or eat a whole orange instead

foods.name: Rum
foods.notes: Pure distilled spirits are FODMAP-free. Same as gin, vodka, whiskey.

foods.name: Soy milk (from soy protein)
foods.notes: Soy milk made from soy protein isolate (not whole soy beans) is Low FODMAP. Check the ingredient list.

foods.name: Erythritol
foods.notes: The only sugar alcohol considered Low FODMAP. Well absorbed in the small intestine unlike sorbitol/mannitol.

foods.name: Garlic-infused oil
foods.notes: FODMAPs from garlic are water-soluble and do not leach into oil - safe for all FODMAP types.

foods.name: High-fructose corn syrup
foods.notes: Common hidden ingredient; check condiment, sauce, and drink labels carefully.

foods.name: Hummus
foods.notes: Low at up to 2 tbsp (42g). Larger servings are High due to chickpea GOS and often garlic.

foods.name: Peanut butter
foods.notes: Check for added high-fructose corn syrup or honey in commercial brands.

foods.name: Pesto sauce
foods.notes: Low at less than 1 tbsp due to garlic content. A normal pasta-sauce quantity is High - use garlic-infused oil based pesto where possible.

foods.name: Soy sauce
foods.notes: Traditional soy sauce is low FODMAP at this serving; check for added wheat.

foods.name: Sucralose (Splenda)
foods.notes: Artificial sweetener; safe on a low-FODMAP diet. However, some Splenda products contain maltodextrin or other fillers.

foods.name: Sugar (white)
foods.notes: Balanced glucose-to-fructose ratio makes it low FODMAP at typical servings.

foods.name: Coconut cream
foods.notes: Low at up to 1/4 cup. Larger amounts used in rich curries may push into moderate territory.
